items.evidence: "Moritz presented the wooden, customizable remote" - the notes use this name consistently for the User Interface Designer, who gave the presentation.
"A flip-panel LCD is included provisionally" and "The back and flip case could have customized designs."

The notes cover the Project Manager's cost sheet ("€9.95 against a €12.50 budget", component list, "LCD price was not included; adding it could cost about €2–€3"). The transcript does not show a decision that the budget rules out the LCD. The Marketing Expert says adding it brings the cost to about 12-12.5, and the Industrial Designer says "we can put the LCD in". The notes only say the LCD put feasibility in doubt.

"Negotiate lower production costs with vendors and discuss cost reductions with management (owner: Speaker 1)". In the transcript the Project Manager ties the savings to marketing and promotion, not to the display, so the notes match the transcript.

"The market study estimated annual demand at eight million units... Selling two million units in year one would require 25% of the market" and "The group questioned whether the company could reach its two-million-unit and €50 million profit targets."
"Christine proposed online ordering and direct shipment as an alternative sales channel", with Amazon/eBay and online customization images.

"Moritz said the project had no redesign time if users found problems" and "The company representative chose to keep the basic design for market introduction and use customer feedback for a second generation."
"coordinating a user-tested launch with a major sports event" and "a campaign with Sony Pictures around a DVD release."
Action item: "Negotiate lower production costs with vendors and discuss cost reductions with management (owner: Speaker 1)" - Speaker 1 is the Project Manager.
"Try to convince management to pursue a campaign with Sony Pictures (owner: Speaker 1)". This matches the Project Manager's "I will convince the management to do that".
The notes never say the marketing work is left to the Marketing Expert for after production ("let's leave it to the Ed for later for once production is over").
"Production evaluation was expected in two to four weeks" - the notes mention an evaluation but not that it follows production of real units.

The LCD is "included provisionally", but the notes say "The microphone location was unresolved" and only that the side was "considered". In the transcript the Project Manager accepted the side ("the sides maybe is good. So That's good idea").

The notes say the Project Manager will negotiate lower production costs. The transcript does not tie this to the display (the stated purpose was money for marketing), so the notes are accurate to the transcript.
"Christine suggested coordinating a user-tested launch with a major sports event" and "a campaign with Sony Pictures around a DVD release", with the PM saying he would convince management.
"The company representative chose to keep the basic design for market introduction and use customer feedback for a second generation."

The notes mention an evaluation in two to four weeks and "Production would begin after approval". They do not state that evaluation waits for real units. The transcript is itself muddled ("prototype product evaluation").

The notes cover the profit-goal doubt ("put feasibility in doubt", 25% market share needed). They do not state that budget plans must change. The transcript shows the LCD roughly fits the €12.50 budget.
"wanted to proceed with the current design, while the others argued for user testing and enough time to respond."

errors.claim: Prototypes would be made outside the company's factory.
errors.why_wrong: The Project Manager said the product evaluation would not be done in their factory ("we are not going to do it in our factory, so we can give it a product evaluation"). He said nothing about where prototypes would be made.

errors.claim: Christine estimated the case could cost €1 for material and labor.
errors.why_wrong: The €1 case cost was on the Project Manager's cost sheet. The Industrial Designer was only commenting on it ("you got some pretty cheap labour that can do this case for one Euro").

errors.claim: Moritz presented the wooden, customizable remote (User Interface Designer called Moritz throughout).
errors.why_wrong: The name Moritz never appears in the transcript. The agenda names the presenters as Christine and Agnes, and the presenter says "Christine can just correct me", so the User Interface Designer is Agnes.
